answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. The design works because cost compounds over compute, time, and reputation, growing faster than the influence the cluster can extract. The effect is that voting power tracks real contribution, so a flood of accounts cannot outvote a smaller set of genuinely established participants. Consider a oasis as the anchor of the cost.
